text:
Maria C: quick sync — uploaded the KV/cache microbench we ran against latest kernels, curious about p95 changes after the kernel switch. logs + script in the GCS link.
Ajay: link?
Maria C: gs://redwood-perf/artifacts/kv-microbench/1932104567.tar.gz :point_up: contains replay traces + synthetic harness we used, and the runner config (microbatch=4, max_batch_width=8)
Kevin L: saw a ~12% p95 regression on the new kernel on the replay, but synthetic runs looked fine. suspect KV eviction jitter under concurrency.
Sophia R: do we have the tail per-model breakdown? p99 mostly stable?
Maria C: p99 was mostly unchanged for short seqs (<128) but for long seqs (512+) p95 shifted a lot. attached a sampling of the flamegraphs in the archive.
Ajay: important to call out that our replay traffic has higher prefix reuse, so KV cache hit rate is 74% in replay vs 40% in synthetic. that changes batching dynamics.
Kevin L: yeah, when KV hit rate is high we hit the KV read path more frequently for cache warming and it serializes some parts of kernel selection. new kernel introduced a small lock around the fused-kv loader.
Sophia R: can you paste the hotspot stack?
Maria C: ```
0x7fabc kernel_fused_kv_loader
0x7fdef exec_attention
0x7ff12 schedule_batch
```
Maria C: the lock is in fused_kv_loader::ensure_loaded (tiny critical section) but with microbatch=4 and lots of prefix reuse it becomes visible.
Ajay: suggestion: re-run with microbatch=2 and also try continuous-batching=false to isolate kernel scheduling vs batching.
Kevin L: also try bumping max_batch_width to 16 to see if convoying reduces tail.
perf-bot: run queued: perf/1932104567/retry-1 (microbatch=2,max_batch_width=16,continuous_batching=false)
Sophia R: question for folks: when we report p95/p99 in benchmarks do we prefer replay-derived p95 (realistic but biased by cache) or synthetic p95 (controlled but underestimates cache effects)?
Ajay: both but labeled. replay for production SLOs, synthetic for kernel/regression isolation. we need a formal rubric: replay_primary, synthetic_control.
Kevin L: agree. also add an explicit KV-hit-rate dimension to summaries. p95 should be stratified by KV-hit bucket: [0-25,25-50,50-75,75-100].
Maria C: okay i'll re-run with Ajay's config, collect per-batch-width histograms, and post a compact table. goal: reproduce regression with microbatch changes then isolate whether removing the lock is necessary.
Sophia R: if repro holds, we need a small kernel patch to move the loader out of the critical path. file an RFC and tag eng-runtime.
Maria C: noted. thanks y'all, will post results later today :thumbsup:
